document.title: Machine Learning Foundations
document.overview: A curated introductory learning graph for machine learning foundations, designed by a learning experience designer and supported with visual resources.

topics.title: What Is Machine Learning?
topics.summary: Machine learning teaches computers to find patterns in data for prediction or decision-making instead of relying only on explicit rules.
topics.context: Introduces models, predictions, training, inference, and major families of machine learning.

topics.title: Data, Features, Labels, and Datasets
topics.summary: Machine learning works with datasets made of examples, features, and, in supervised learning, labels.
topics.context: Builds the vocabulary needed before discussing model training and evaluation.

topics.title: Supervised Learning
topics.summary: Supervised learning trains a model on labeled examples to map inputs to outputs, usually for regression or classification.
topics.context: Connects labeled data to model training, loss, and prediction.

topics.title: Train, Validation, and Test Splits
topics.summary: Datasets are split so models can be trained, tuned, and finally evaluated on data they have not seen before.
topics.context: Explains why reliable evaluation requires separating development data from final test data.

topics.title: Preparing Data for Machine Learning
topics.summary: Before modeling, data often needs missing-value handling, scaling, categorical encoding, feature engineering, and consistent preprocessing.
topics.context: Shows how raw data becomes usable model input.

topics.title: Overfitting, Underfitting, and Generalization
topics.summary: A model should work on new data, not just training data; overfitting and underfitting describe two common failures.
topics.context: Introduces generalization, model complexity, and the bias-variance tradeoff.

concepts.title: Model
concepts.summary: A learned mapping from inputs to outputs.
concepts.context: The model is the object trained from data and then used to make predictions.

concepts.title: Prediction
concepts.summary: The output a model produces for a given input.
concepts.context: Predictions are compared with desired outcomes during training or used directly during inference.

concepts.title: Training
concepts.summary: The process of improving a model from examples.
concepts.context: Training adjusts the model so its predictions become more useful on future inputs.

concepts.title: Inference
concepts.summary: Using a trained model to make predictions.
concepts.context: Inference is the application phase after a model has already learned from data.

concepts.title: Supervised Learning
concepts.summary: Learning from examples that include known correct answers.
concepts.context: Supervised learning is one of the main families of machine learning.

media.caption: A labeled example contains input features and a known target label.
media.placement: Use when introducing supervised learning or labels.

media.caption: A model first makes a prediction from a labeled example.
media.placement: Use when explaining the first step of training.

concepts.title: Unsupervised Learning
concepts.summary: Learning patterns from data without known labels.
concepts.context: Unsupervised learning is useful when the structure in the data is unknown.

media.caption: An unlabeled example contains input features without a known target label.
media.placement: Use when contrasting unsupervised learning with supervised learning.

concepts.title: Example
concepts.summary: One row, case, observation, or instance in a dataset.
concepts.context: Examples are the individual units a model learns from or predicts on.

concepts.title: Feature
concepts.summary: An input variable that describes an example.
concepts.context: Features are the information the model uses to make predictions.

concepts.title: Label
concepts.summary: The known target answer for a supervised learning example.
concepts.context: Labels let supervised models compare predictions with correct outcomes.

concepts.title: Dataset
concepts.summary: A collection of examples used for learning or evaluation.
concepts.context: Datasets organize examples, features, and labels into material a model can use.

concepts.title: Numerical Feature
concepts.summary: A feature represented by numbers with meaningful magnitude.
concepts.context: Numerical features often need scaling or distribution checks before modeling.

media.caption: A numerical feature can be inspected through its distribution.
media.placement: Use when contrasting numerical and categorical features.

concepts.title: Categorical Feature
concepts.summary: A feature represented by categories rather than magnitude.
concepts.context: Categorical features usually need encoding before many models can use them.

media.caption: A categorical feature has discrete category values.

concepts.title: Regression
concepts.summary: A supervised learning task that predicts a numeric value.
concepts.context: Regression is used when the target has ordered numeric magnitude.

concepts.title: Classification
concepts.summary: A supervised learning task that predicts a category.
concepts.context: Classification is used when the model chooses among discrete classes.

concepts.title: Loss
concepts.summary: A measure of how wrong a model prediction is.
concepts.context: Loss gives the training process a signal for how to improve the model.

media.caption: Prediction error is converted into a learning signal.
media.placement: Use when introducing loss during supervised training.

concepts.title: Training Loop
concepts.summary: Repeated prediction, error measurement, and model update.
concepts.context: The supervised training loop gradually improves model parameters over many examples.

media.caption: Training repeats prediction, loss calculation, and update.
media.placement: Use when explaining how supervised learning improves over time.

concepts.title: Training Set
concepts.summary: Data used to fit model parameters.
concepts.context: The model directly learns from the training set.

concepts.title: Validation Set
concepts.summary: Data used during development to tune choices and compare models.
concepts.context: Validation data helps choose model settings without touching the final test set.

concepts.title: Test Set
concepts.summary: Held-out data used for final evaluation.
concepts.context: The test set estimates how the finished model performs on unseen data.

media.caption: A common split separates training, validation, and test data.
media.placement: Use when explaining why evaluation data must be separated.

concepts.title: Generalization Estimate
concepts.summary: An estimate of performance on data the model has not seen.
concepts.context: Good evaluation tries to approximate future performance, not memorized training performance.

media.caption: Model evaluation compares predictions on held-out data with true answers.
media.placement: Use when connecting test performance to generalization.

concepts.title: Missing Values
concepts.summary: Absent or unknown feature values that must be handled before modeling.
concepts.context: Missing data can break models or bias results if ignored.

concepts.title: Feature Scaling
concepts.summary: Transforming numerical features onto comparable ranges.
concepts.context: Scaling helps models that are sensitive to feature magnitude.

concepts.title: One-Hot Encoding
concepts.summary: Representing categories as indicator columns.
concepts.context: One-hot encoding converts categorical values into numeric model inputs.

concepts.title: Feature Engineering
concepts.summary: Creating useful model inputs from raw data.
concepts.context: Feature engineering can make important patterns easier for a model to learn.

concepts.title: Preprocessing Consistency
concepts.summary: Applying the same preprocessing during training and inference.
concepts.context: A model can fail if production inputs are transformed differently from training inputs.

concepts.title: Overfitting
concepts.summary: When a model fits training data too closely and performs poorly on new data.
concepts.context: Overfitting means the model has learned noise or accidental patterns rather than durable structure.

media.caption: Overfitting and underfitting show different failures of model complexity.
media.placement: Use when contrasting model fit with generalization.

concepts.title: Underfitting
concepts.summary: When a model is too simple to capture the important pattern.
concepts.context: Underfitting usually produces poor performance on both training and test data.

media.caption: Underfitting appears when the model cannot capture the underlying structure.

concepts.title: Generalization
concepts.summary: The ability to perform well on new examples.
concepts.context: Generalization is the central goal of model evaluation and regularization.

concepts.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
concepts.summary: The tension between models that are too simple and models that are too sensitive.
concepts.context: The tradeoff explains why both underfitting and overfitting can hurt performance.

concepts.title: Regularization
concepts.summary: A technique that discourages overly complex models.
concepts.context: Regularization helps reduce overfitting and improve generalization.

media.caption: Regularization constrains model complexity to improve generalization.
media.placement: Use when explaining how overfitting can be reduced.
